job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: Teacher: Today, let us discuss how water moves and changes. Rohan, do you think water vapor only exists when we boil water on a stove? Rohan: Yes, I thought it disappears if it doesn't reach boiling point. Teacher: Actually, water evaporates from oceans and even from plants through transpiration, turning into vapor constantly. Priya: Does that mean the water table stays at the same depth forever? Teacher: Not at all, Priya. The water table rises or falls depending on rainfall and how much we pump out. It is not a fixed line. Priya: I once saw a treatment plant and thought it made water 100% pure, removing every single particle. Teacher: That is a common mistake. Treatment plants remove harmful pollutants and germs, but the water still contains dissolved minerals and is not chemically pure. Also, remember that groundwater is not stored in large open underground caves or swimming pools; it fills the tiny spaces between soil particles and rocks. Finally, we must stop thinking that water scarcity is only caused by household waste. Large-scale agriculture and industrial needs also significantly impact our water availability. We must manage these resources carefully to ensure everyone has enough.

items.evidence: The water table rises or falls depending on rainfall and how much we pump out.
items.q: A region gets very little rain for years while people keep pumping water. What happens to its water table?
options: It stays at the same depth
It rises closer to the surface
It moves only when rivers flood
items.explain: The water table rises or falls with rainfall and pumping, so less rain and more pumping lowers it.

wrong.why: thinks the water table never moves
reverses cause and effect of pumping
thinks groundwater behaves like surface rivers

items.evidence: Treatment plants remove harmful pollutants and germs, but the water still contains dissolved minerals and is not chemically pure.
items.q: Water from a treatment plant is safe to drink. Why is it still not chemically pure?
options: It keeps some dissolved minerals in it
It keeps the germs the plant found
It keeps pollutants the plant cannot see
It keeps small particles of the filter
items.explain: Plants remove pollutants and germs, but dissolved minerals remain, so the water is safe but not chemically pure.

wrong.why: thinks treated water still has germs
thinks treatment gives pure water, so only hidden pollutants remain
invents a nearby detail not in the passage

items.evidence: Also, remember that groundwater is not stored in large open underground caves or swimming pools; it fills the tiny spaces between soil particles and rocks.
items.q: How is groundwater stored under the ground?
options: It fills tiny gaps in soil and rock
It collects in huge empty caves
It flows in large underground rivers
It sits in open underground pools
items.explain: Groundwater fills the tiny spaces between soil particles and rocks, not open caves or pools.

wrong.why: thinks groundwater sits in empty underground caves
thinks groundwater is an underground river
thinks groundwater sits in underground pools

items.evidence: Large-scale agriculture and industrial needs also significantly impact our water availability.
items.q: A town's taps run dry though homes waste little water. Which could explain this?
options: Farms and factories use huge amounts of water
Plants stop releasing water into the air
Snow and ice are not real water
The water table is a fixed line
items.explain: Large farms and industries also strongly affect water availability, so scarcity is not caused by homes alone.

wrong.why: thinks plants do not release water, a distant cause
thinks ice and snow are different from water
thinks the water table never moves
